newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iran says U.S. sanctions against it have failed.
newsitem.headline: Iran says U.S. sanctions against it have failed.

text.p: U.S. sanctions against Iran have failed, Iranian deputy foreign minister Abbas Maleki said in an address read on his behalf to an oil industry conference here.
"These sanctions are against the rules and regulations of the World Trade Organisation," said Maleki. "But on the other hand there has been no tangible economic effect on Iran."
Maleki's speech was read by the Iranian Ambassador to Cyprus, Ali Farazi.
The U.S. approved legislation in August which punishes non-U.S. firms investing $40 million or more in Iran's gas and oil industries. The European Union and other states have criticised the move.
Crude oil comprises about 80 percent of Iran's exports.
"Iran's foreign debt is well organised and steps to reduce it are continuing all the time," said Maleki.
Inflation, he said, was slashed to 36.8 percent this year from more than 55 percent in previous years while economic growth is estimated at 45 percent.
"In view of these figures and the fact that we now have new customers for oil the sanctions have had no significant impact on the economy," Maleki said.
